key_insight: Routine clinical data helped shortlist genetic diagnoses in children with congenital heart disease, while multimodal deep learning did not outperform logistic regression.
clinical_relevance: Data available at the first echocardiogram could support earlier recognition of possible genetic conditions, without replacing confirmatory testing.
method: Retrospective, single-center cohort of 1,720 children with congenital heart disease and genetic testing.
Compared class-balanced logistic regression with multimodal deep learning as echocardiogram images and clinical records became available.
Evaluated balanced top-3 accuracy and embedding-based retrieval for genetic conditions withheld from training.
evidence_signal: Logistic regression achieved balanced top-3 accuracy of 0.758 using echocardiogram-visit inputs versus 0.429 chance, rising to 0.809 with serial records, radiology notes and ICD-10 codes.
watch_item: Retrospective results from a single-center, genetically tested cohort require external and prospective validation before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Modeling to Aid in the Identification of Genetic Conditions in Infants with Congenital Heart Disease
